q20835.en: The kerb painted as in the picture forbids parking to taxis too.

explain.short: Yellow and black stripes on the kerb mean no parking for every vehicle. Taxis are no exception.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes on the kerb = no parking for any vehicle.
explain.trap: 'anche ai taxi' (taxis too): the ban is for everybody.

sceneParams.caption: No parking for anyone, taxis included

q20836.en: The kerb painted as in the picture means that no vehicle may park.

explain.short: This kerb marking is a no-parking marking. It applies to all vehicles.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes on the kerb = no parking for any vehicle.
explain.trap: 'nessun veicolo' (no vehicle) is correct: nobody may park here.

sceneParams.caption: No vehicle may park along this kerb

q20837.en: The kerb painted as in the picture means that you may not park along that stretch.

explain.short: Where the kerb has yellow and black stripes, parking is forbidden along that stretch of road.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes on the kerb = no parking for any vehicle.
explain.trap: 'lungo quel tratto' (along that stretch): the ban lasts as long as the painted kerb.

sceneParams.caption: No parking where the kerb is painted

q20838.en: The kerb painted as in the picture means that parking is allowed only if you pay.

explain.short: This kerb means no parking at all. Paid parking is shown with blue lines, not with a yellow and black kerb.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes on the kerb = no parking for any vehicle.
explain.trap: 'solo a pagamento' (only if you pay) is wrong: here you may not park even if you pay.

sceneParams.caption: Not paid parking: no parking at all

q20839.en: The kerb painted as in the picture means that parking is allowed only for one hour.

explain.short: This kerb means no parking at all. It gives no time limit for parking.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes on the kerb = no parking for any vehicle.
explain.trap: 'solo per un'ora' (only for one hour) is wrong: you may not park here for any time.

sceneParams.caption: No time limit: parking is simply forbidden

q20840.en: The kerb painted as in the picture shows that there are road works.

explain.short: This kerb only means no parking. Road works are shown by warning signs and by temporary yellow markings on the road.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes on the kerb = no parking for any vehicle.
explain.trap: 'lavori in corso' (road works) has nothing to do with this kerb.

sceneParams.caption: Not road works: it means no parking

q20841.en: The kerb painted as in the picture shows a road with right of way.

explain.short: This kerb only means no parking. A priority road is shown by a vertical sign, not by the kerb.
explain.rule: Yellow and black stripes on the kerb = no parking for any vehicle.
explain.trap: 'diritto di precedenza' (right of way) is wrong: the kerb says nothing about priority.

sceneParams.caption: Not a priority road: it means no parking

q20842.en: It is regular to find the word BUS in yellow on the road surface in areas for stopping public bus services.

explain.short: Yellow is used for reserved areas. The yellow word BUS marks the place where line buses stop.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'di colore giallo' (yellow) is right: reserved areas use yellow markings.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow BUS: the bus stop area

q20843.en: It is regular to find the word TAXI in yellow on the road surface to show areas reserved for parking of taxis in service.

explain.short: Taxi parking areas are reserved, so they are marked in yellow with the word TAXI.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'di colore giallo' (yellow) is the key: a reserved taxi area uses yellow.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow TAXI: parking for taxis only

q20844.en: It is regular to find the word STOP on the road surface, to complete the matching vertical sign.

explain.short: The word STOP painted on the road helps the STOP sign. It is placed just before the stop line.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'a completamento' (to complete): the writing adds to the STOP sign, it does not replace it.

sceneParams.caption: STOP on the road completes the STOP sign

q20845.en: It is regular to find the letters P L on the road surface, with a St Andrew's cross, to warn of a level crossing.

explain.short: Before a level crossing (passaggio a livello, railway crossing) the road can show P L with a St Andrew's cross (an X shape).
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'P L' stands for 'passaggio a livello' (level crossing).

sceneParams.caption: P L + cross on the road: level crossing ahead
lines: P L with an X on the road

q20846.en: When you meet the stripes in the picture painted on the road, you must reduce speed.

explain.short: These white bars across the lane get closer and closer. They make you feel fast, so you slow down before a danger.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'moderare la velocità' (reduce speed) is exactly what these bars ask.

sceneParams.caption: Bars across the lane: slow down

q20847.en: It is regular to find on the road surface the name of a place, to complete the direction arrow.

explain.short: A place name can be painted next to a direction arrow. It shows which lane goes to that town.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'a completamento della freccia' (to complete the arrow): the name helps you pick the lane.

sceneParams.caption: Place name + arrow: choose your lane

q20848.en: It is regular to find the word STOP on the road surface, to complete the vertical GIVE WAY sign.

explain.short: The word STOP goes only with the STOP sign. With GIVE WAY you find a dashed line and white triangles, not STOP.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'DARE PRECEDENZA' (give way) is the wrong sign: STOP and give way are different.

sceneParams.caption: STOP writing goes with STOP, not GIVE WAY

q20849.en: It is regular to find on the road surface writing that shows a service station coming up.

explain.short: Road writings only complete official signs. Telling you about a service station is not one of their jobs.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'stazione di servizio' (service station) is not an allowed road writing.

sceneParams.caption: No service-station writing on the road

q20850.en: It is regular to find advertising writing on the road surface for a petrol station.

explain.short: Advertising on the road surface is never allowed. It distracts drivers and is not a road sign.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'pubblicitaria' (advertising) makes it wrong: no adverts on the road.

sceneParams.caption: No adverts painted on the road

q20851.en: It is regular to find writing on the road surface cheering on cycle racers.

explain.short: Road writings are only for traffic information. Messages for cyclists in a race are not road signs.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'incoraggiamento' (cheering) is not a traffic message, so it is not allowed.

sceneParams.caption: No cheering messages on the road

q20852.en: It is regular to find the word TAXI in white on the road surface in taxi parking areas.

explain.short: Taxi areas are reserved, and reserved areas use yellow. A white TAXI is not the right marking.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'di colore bianco' (white) is the trap: the word TAXI must be yellow.

sceneParams.caption: TAXI must be yellow, not white

q20853.en: It is regular to find the word GIOCHI (games) on the road surface near public gardens.

explain.short: GIOCHI is not an allowed road writing. Children near a park are announced by the vertical CHILDREN warning sign.
explain.rule: Road writings only complete official signs: BUS, TAXI (yellow), STOP, P L, place names.
explain.trap: 'GIOCHI' (games/playground) is not in the list of allowed road writings.

sceneParams.caption: GIOCHI is not an allowed road writing
lines: GIOCHI on the road: not allowed

q20854.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may overtake even by crossing the centre line.

explain.short: The dashed line separates two lanes going the same way. You may cross a dashed line to overtake.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'superando la striscia di mezzo' (crossing the centre line) is fine because it is dashed.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line: you may cross it to overtake

q20855.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may overtake even on a bend.

explain.short: Nobody comes towards you on a one-way road with two lanes. So overtaking on a bend is allowed.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'anche in curva' (even on a bend) sounds wrong, but on a one-way road it is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: One-way, 2 lanes: overtaking on a bend is OK

q20856.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, the carriageway is divided into two lanes.

explain.short: The dashed line in the middle splits the carriageway into two lanes, both going the same way.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'due corsie' (two lanes): one line in the middle makes two lanes.

sceneParams.caption: One dashed line = two lanes

q20857.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, the left lane is, as a rule, reserved for overtaking.

explain.short: You normally drive in the right lane. The left lane is, as a rule, used to overtake.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule) makes it true: it is the normal use, with some exceptions like turning left.

sceneParams.caption: Drive right, use the left lane to overtake

q20858.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, overtaking near or on humps is allowed.

explain.short: Near a hump (dosso, crest of a hill) you cannot see ahead, but on a one-way road nobody comes towards you. So overtaking is allowed.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'dossi' (humps) usually ban overtaking, but not on a one-way road with two lanes.

sceneParams.caption: One-way, 2 lanes: overtaking near a hump is OK

q20859.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may always drive in parallel rows.

explain.short: Side by side driving (file parallele) is allowed only when traffic is heavy. Normally you keep to the right lane.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is the trap: parallel rows are not always allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Side by side only in heavy traffic, not always
lines: Side by side: only in heavy traffic

q20860.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may do a U-turn.

explain.short: A U-turn on a one-way road would make you drive against the traffic. It is forbidden.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'inversione del senso di marcia' (U-turn) is never allowed on a one-way road.

sceneParams.caption: No U-turn on a one-way road

q20861.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may drive straddling the centre line.

explain.short: You must drive inside a lane. Driving on top of the line (a cavallo) is never allowed.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'a cavallo' (straddling) is forbidden on any lane line, dashed or solid.

sceneParams.caption: Never drive on top of the lane line

q20862.en: On a one-way road with the markings shown in the picture, to turn left you must stay in the right lane.

explain.short: On a one-way road you turn left from the left lane. You move to the left side before the turn.
explain.rule: One-way road, dashed line: two lanes the same way; cross it to overtake, even on bends.
explain.trap: 'rimanere nella corsia di destra' (stay in the right lane) is wrong for a left turn.

sceneParams.caption: Turning left: move to the left lane
lines: Turn left: use the left lane

q20863.en: The markings in the picture show a pedestrian crossing, both inside and outside built-up areas.

explain.short: Zebra stripes are a pedestrian crossing everywhere: in towns and on out-of-town roads.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'sia dentro che fuori' (both inside and outside) is right: zebras are used everywhere.

sceneParams.caption: Zebra crossing: in town and outside

q20864.en: The markings in the picture show a pedestrian crossing that can be found in small towns too.

explain.short: A pedestrian crossing can be anywhere pedestrians cross, small towns included.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'anche nei piccoli centri' (in small towns too) is correct: there is no size limit.

sceneParams.caption: Zebra crossings: small towns too

q20865.en: The markings in the picture show a pedestrian crossing.

explain.short: Wide white stripes parallel to the road (zebras) mark a pedestrian crossing.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'attraversamento pedonale' (pedestrian crossing) is the correct name.

sceneParams.caption: Zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing

q20866.en: The markings in the picture show a crossing for pedestrians.

explain.short: These zebra stripes are where people on foot cross the road.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'per pedoni' (for pedestrians) is the same as 'pedonale'.

sceneParams.caption: Zebra stripes: crossing for pedestrians

q20867.en: The markings in the picture show a crossing where pedestrians have priority.

explain.short: On a zebra crossing pedestrians go first. Drivers must give way to them.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'hanno la precedenza' (have priority) is right: pedestrians first.

sceneParams.caption: On zebras pedestrians go first

q20868.en: The markings in the picture show a traffic island.

explain.short: A traffic island is a raised or striped area where you may not drive. Zebras are a crossing on the road you drive on.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'isola di traffico' (traffic island) is a different marking (diagonal stripes with a border).

sceneParams.caption: Not an island: a pedestrian crossing

q20869.en: The markings in the picture show a crossing for cyclists.

explain.short: A cycle crossing is marked by two dashed lines (small squares), not by zebra stripes.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'per ciclisti' (for cyclists) is wrong: zebras are for pedestrians.

sceneParams.caption: Zebras are for pedestrians, not cyclists

q20870.en: The markings in the picture show a cycle crossing.

explain.short: A cycle crossing has two lines of small white squares. Zebra stripes are a pedestrian crossing.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'ciclabile' (for bicycles) is wrong for zebra stripes.

sceneParams.caption: Not a cycle crossing: a pedestrian crossing

q20871.en: The markings in the picture show a driveway.

explain.short: A driveway (passo carrabile, an entrance for vehicles) is shown by a vertical sign, not by zebra stripes.
explain.rule: White zebra stripes = pedestrian crossing, pedestrians have priority.
explain.trap: 'passo carrabile' (driveway) has nothing to do with zebras.

sceneParams.caption: Not a driveway: a pedestrian crossing

q20872.en: The white transverse line in the picture can be used at a junction controlled by traffic lights.

explain.short: At traffic lights the solid line across the lane shows where you stop when the light is red.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'semaforo' (traffic light): the stop line is used there too, not only with STOP.

sceneParams.caption: Stop line: also at traffic lights

q20873.en: The white transverse line in the picture can be completed by the word STOP painted on the road.

explain.short: Before a STOP line the word STOP may be painted on the road, to help the STOP sign.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'scritta STOP' (word STOP) fits a stop line, unlike a give-way line.

sceneParams.caption: Stop line + STOP written on the road

q20874.en: The white transverse line in the picture shows the point where drivers must stop when there is a STOP (STOP AND GIVE WAY) sign.

explain.short: With a STOP sign you must stop completely at this solid line, then give way.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'FERMARSI E DARE PRECEDENZA' is the full name of the STOP sign, which uses a solid line.

sceneParams.caption: STOP sign: stop at the solid line

q20875.en: The white transverse line in the picture shows the point where drivers must stop when the traffic light is red.

explain.short: When the light is red you stop before this solid line, not after it.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'luce rossa' (red light): the stop line tells you exactly where to stop.

sceneParams.caption: Red light: stop before the line

q20876.en: The sign shown is a transverse stop line.

explain.short: A solid white line across the lane is called a stop line (striscia di arresto).
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'striscia trasversale di arresto' (transverse stop line) is the correct name.

sceneParams.caption: Solid line across the lane = stop line

q20877.en: The white transverse line in the picture is used with the GIVE WAY sign.

explain.short: With GIVE WAY the line across the lane is dashed, not solid. The solid line goes with STOP or traffic lights.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'DARE PRECEDENZA' (give way) uses a dashed line, so the solid line is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Give way = dashed line; this solid line = STOP
lines: Solid line: STOP or red light

q20878.en: The white transverse line in the picture shows an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing.

explain.short: A pedestrian crossing is shown by zebra stripes. A single solid line across the lane is a stop line.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'attraversamento pedonale' (pedestrian crossing) needs zebra stripes, not one line.

sceneParams.caption: One solid line is a stop line, not zebras

q20879.en: The white transverse line in the picture shows a cycle crossing.

explain.short: A cycle crossing has two lines of small white squares. This single solid line is a stop line.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'attraversamento ciclabile' (cycle crossing) is a different marking.

sceneParams.caption: Not a cycle crossing: a stop line

q20880.en: The white transverse line in the picture may never be crossed.

explain.short: You stop at the line, then you cross it when you can go: after giving way or when the light is green.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'non può mai' (may never) is the trap: you stop at it, you do not stay there forever.

sceneParams.caption: Stop at the line, then go when it is clear

q20881.en: The white transverse line in the picture shows the start of a no-parking zone.

explain.short: A line across the lane tells you where to stop at a junction. It says nothing about parking.
explain.rule: Solid transverse line = stop line for a STOP sign or a red light.
explain.trap: 'divieto di sosta' (no parking) has nothing to do with the stop line.

sceneParams.caption: Stop line is not a no-parking marking
lines: Line across the lane: stop here

q20882.en: On a two-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may overtake even by crossing the centre line.

explain.short: The centre line is dashed, so you may cross it to overtake when the other lane is free.
explain.rule: Two-way road, dashed line: you may cross it to overtake when it is safe; never straddle it.
explain.trap: 'superando la striscia di mezzo' (crossing the centre line) is OK because it is dashed.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed centre line: may cross to overtake
lines: Cross it to overtake if free

q20883.en: On a two-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may not drive straddling the centre line.

explain.short: You must drive inside your lane. Driving on top of the centre line is forbidden.
explain.rule: Two-way road, dashed line: you may cross it to overtake when it is safe; never straddle it.
explain.trap: 'non si può' (you may not) makes it true: straddling is never allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Never drive on top of the centre line

q20884.en: On a two-way road with the markings shown in the picture, to turn left you must move towards the centre of the carriageway.

explain.short: Before a left turn on a two-way road you move close to the centre line, staying in your lane.
explain.rule: Two-way road, dashed line: you may cross it to overtake when it is safe; never straddle it.
explain.trap: 'verso il centro' (towards the centre) is right for a left turn on a two-way road.

sceneParams.caption: Turning left: move near the centre line
lines: Left turn on a two-way road

q20885.en: On a two-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may overtake in any visibility and traffic conditions.

explain.short: A dashed line allows overtaking only when you can see well and the road is free. In fog or with oncoming cars you may not.
explain.rule: Two-way road, dashed line: you may cross it to overtake when it is safe; never straddle it.
explain.trap: 'qualsiasi condizione' (any conditions) is the trap: safety conditions always count.

sceneParams.caption: Overtake only with good view and free road

q20886.en: On a two-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may overtake even on a bend, but only in town.

explain.short: On a two-way road with one lane each way, overtaking on a bend is forbidden, in town and outside.
explain.rule: Two-way road, dashed line: you may cross it to overtake when it is safe; never straddle it.
explain.trap: 'ma solo in città' (but only in town) is invented: the ban on bends is everywhere.

sceneParams.caption: No overtaking on a bend, in town too

q20887.en: On a two-way road with the markings shown in the picture, you may do a U-turn, but without occupying the other lane.

explain.short: With one lane each way, a U-turn always uses the other lane. You do it only when it is free and the line is dashed.
explain.rule: Two-way road, dashed line: you may cross it to overtake when it is safe; never straddle it.
explain.trap: 'senza occupare l'altra corsia' (without using the other lane) is impossible here.

sceneParams.caption: A U-turn here always uses the other lane

q20888.en: On a two-way road with the markings shown in the picture, outside built-up areas the left lane is for emergency stops.

explain.short: On a two-way road the left lane is for traffic coming towards you. For emergencies you stop on the right, off the carriageway if possible.
explain.rule: Two-way road, dashed line: you may cross it to overtake when it is safe; never straddle it.
explain.trap: 'sosta d'emergenza' (emergency stop) in the left lane is wrong and dangerous.

sceneParams.caption: Left lane = oncoming traffic, not emergencies

q20889.en: On a two-way carriageway the centre line can be solid or broken (dashed).

explain.short: The centre line is dashed where overtaking is possible and solid where it is dangerous.
explain.rule: Dashed centre line: may be crossed. Solid (single or double): never crossed.
explain.trap: 'può essere' (can be): both types exist.

sceneParams.caption: Centre line: solid or dashed

q20890.en: On a two-way carriageway the centre line, if broken (dashed), may be crossed during an overtake.

explain.short: A dashed centre line may be crossed to overtake, when the road is free and you can see well.
explain.rule: Dashed centre line: may be crossed. Solid (single or double): never crossed.
explain.trap: 'se discontinua' (if broken) is the key: only the dashed line may be crossed.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed centre line: cross it to overtake

q20891.en: On a two-way carriageway the centre line can be made of two solid lines side by side, as in the picture.

explain.short: A double solid line in the middle is allowed. It gives a stronger separation between the two directions.
explain.rule: Dashed centre line: may be crossed. Solid (single or double): never crossed.
explain.trap: 'due strisce continue affiancate' (two solid lines side by side) is a real marking.

sceneParams.caption: Double solid centre line exists
lines: Two solid lines in the middle

q20892.en: On a two-way carriageway the centre line, if made of solid lines as in the picture, allows overtaking without crossing the lines.

explain.short: You may not cross solid lines. But you may overtake if you stay in your lane, for example passing a bicycle.
explain.rule: Dashed centre line: may be crossed. Solid (single or double): never crossed.
explain.trap: 'senza superare le linee' (without crossing the lines) is the key: overtaking is OK only inside your lane.

sceneParams.caption: Overtake only if you stay in your lane

q20893.en: On the two-way carriageway, the centre lines in the picture divide the directions of travel.

explain.short: The lines in the middle separate the traffic going one way from the traffic going the other way.
explain.rule: Dashed centre line: may be crossed. Solid (single or double): never crossed.
explain.trap: 'dividono i sensi di marcia' (divide the directions) is exactly their job.

sceneParams.caption: Centre lines separate the two directions

q20894.en: On the two-way carriageway, the centre line in the picture may be crossed with only the left wheels.

explain.short: The centre line in the picture is solid. A solid line may not be crossed, not even partly with the left wheels.
explain.rule: Dashed centre line: may be crossed. Solid (single or double): never crossed.
explain.trap: 'con le sole ruote di sinistra' (with only the left wheels) is still crossing it.

sceneParams.caption: Solid line: not even with the left wheels

q20895.en: On the two-way carriageway as in the picture, the centre line divides the road into two carriageways, each with two lanes.

explain.short: The picture is one carriageway with one lane each way. A painted line divides lanes; separate carriageways need a divider.
explain.rule: Dashed centre line: may be crossed. Solid (single or double): never crossed.
explain.trap: 'due carreggiate, ognuna a due corsie' (two carriageways, each with two lanes) is wrong: it is one carriageway, two lanes.

sceneParams.caption: One carriageway, one lane each way

q20896.en: The markings in the picture can be completed with the vertical PEDESTRIAN CROSSING sign.

explain.short: A zebra crossing can also have the blue square sign PEDESTRIAN CROSSING next to it.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'può essere completata' (can be completed): the vertical sign adds to the zebras.

sceneParams.caption: Zebras + blue PEDESTRIAN CROSSING sign

q20897.en: The markings in the picture oblige drivers to stop when there are pedestrians crossing the road.

explain.short: If pedestrians are crossing on the zebras, you must stop and let them pass.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'obbliga ad arrestarsi' (obliges to stop) is right when pedestrians are crossing.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrians crossing: you must stop

q20898.en: A pedestrian crossing can be preceded on the right by a yellow zig-zag line, as in the next picture.

explain.short: The picture shows a yellow zig-zag on the right just before the zebras. It is allowed and marks the space before the crossing to keep clear.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'striscia gialla a zig zag' (yellow zig-zag line) can really come before a crossing.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow zig-zag on the right before the zebras

q20898.reviewNote: Unsure of the exact legal meaning of the yellow zig-zag before a crossing; explained only as 'space to keep clear'.

q20899.en: The markings in the picture, on secondary out-of-town roads, must be preceded by the PEDESTRIAN CROSSING danger sign.

explain.short: Outside towns drivers go faster. So on secondary out-of-town roads a danger sign must warn of the crossing before you reach it.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'deve essere preceduta' (must be preceded): outside towns the warning sign is required.

sceneParams.caption: Out of town: danger sign before the zebras

q20900.en: The markings in the picture oblige drivers to stop and give way to pedestrians who are about to cross.

explain.short: You must give way not only to pedestrians on the zebras, but also to those who are just going to step onto them.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'si accingono ad attraversare' (are about to cross) counts too, not only people already crossing.

sceneParams.caption: Give way to people about to cross too

q20901.en: The markings in the picture are a refuge island for pedestrians and cyclists.

explain.short: A refuge island is a safe area in the middle of the road. Zebras are a crossing on the road itself.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'isola di rifugio' (refuge island) is a different thing from a crossing.

sceneParams.caption: Zebras are a crossing, not a refuge island

q20902.en: The markings in the picture do not allow vehicles to drive over them.

explain.short: Vehicles drive over zebras normally. They only have to give way to pedestrians.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'non consente ai veicoli' (does not allow vehicles) is wrong: vehicles may pass when it is free.

sceneParams.caption: Vehicles may cross the zebras when free

q20903.en: The markings in the picture show an area reserved only for disabled pedestrians.

explain.short: A zebra crossing is for all pedestrians, not only disabled people.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'ai soli pedoni disabili' (only disabled pedestrians) is the trap: it is for everyone on foot.

sceneParams.caption: Zebras are for all pedestrians

q20904.en: The markings in the picture do not allow pedestrians to pass.

explain.short: Zebras are made for pedestrians to cross the road. It is the opposite of a ban.
explain.rule: At zebra stripes you stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.
explain.trap: 'non consente il transito ai pedoni' (does not let pedestrians pass) is the opposite of the truth.

sceneParams.caption: Zebras are where pedestrians cross
